# Reproducibility as a Discipline: Every Number in This Project, Rerunnable

### If a claim can't be regenerated by rerunning a script against the same source file, it doesn't get published as VERIFIED

A number in a research write-up is either a fact you can check or a fact you have to take on faith. This project is built around minimizing how much of it falls into the second category.

## What "reproducible" means here, concretely

Every VERIFIED-tier claim in this project traces back to a specific script, in the repository, that anyone can run against the same publicly described raw data structure to get the same result. Not "trust me, I ran some analysis." An actual file, with actual logic, sitting in `/analysis`, that produces the number when executed.

This isn't a nice-to-have bolted on afterward. It shapes how the work gets done in the first place. A finding that can only be produced by manual spreadsheet manipulation, eyeballing, or a one-off interactive session that wasn't saved as a script doesn't get to carry the VERIFIED label, because nobody, including this project's own author, a month later, could actually rerun it to check.

## The discipline this creates

Writing a script instead of doing ad-hoc analysis is slower in the moment. It's also the only way to catch your own mistakes before publishing them. A script's logic can be read, questioned, and re-run with a fix, in a way that a half-remembered manual process can't. Several of this project's own corrections, documented elsewhere in this series, were caught specifically because a script existed to rerun.

## Why this matters more for surprising numbers than boring ones

Nobody double-checks the numbers that confirm what they already expected. The temptation to skip verification is strongest exactly when a finding is most attention-grabbing: the biggest anomaly, the most damning ratio, the number that makes the best headline. That's precisely when a rerunnable script matters most, because it's the only thing standing between "this looks alarming" and "this is alarming and also correct."

## What this is, and isn't

**A standing practice, not a claim about any single number**: every script behind a VERIFIED claim in this project is in the public repository, with its inputs and logic visible.

**A limit, honestly stated**: reproducibility proves the computation is correct given the input. It doesn't independently verify that the underlying raw data itself is accurate or complete. That's a separate, STATED-tier question about the data's own provenance.

Full script index: **github.com/DreamITSoftware/SPOTAPOD**.
